title: Wireless networks & IoT
description: Making wireless communication more efficient, adaptive, and useful in resource-constrained environments.
long: This direction investigates how devices share spectrum, coordinate transmissions, and communicate with limited energy. Work spans fine-grained channel access, LoRa and backscatter communication, mobile and vehicular networks, and learning-based resource management.

title: Intelligent & ubiquitous sensing
description: Turning light, vibration, and radio signals into practical ways to understand the physical world.
long: Everyday signals can reveal information that is difficult to observe directly. This research builds sensing systems for toothbrushing, liquid and food analysis, environmental monitoring, activity recognition, and plant health, combining physical models with signal processing and machine learning.

title: Human-centered computing
description: Designing accessible interfaces and AI systems that people can understand, guide, and use with confidence.
long: This work examines how people interact with small devices and intelligent systems. Projects include assistive headphones, wearable text entry, music understanding, and interactive AI tools for meeting summaries and contract review. The emphasis is on useful capabilities, transparent interaction, and user control.
